title: The Deer-eyed Girl's Multiplication
devanagari: छिन्नास्तेन गुणेन ते च गुणिता जाताः कति स्युर्वद॥
translation: O girl, Lilavati, with eyes as restless as a young deer's! If you are clever, O fair one, at multiplying whole, by places, by factors and by parts, tell me: the number written five-three-one, multiplied by the suns, what does it become? And when that product is divided by the same multiplier, what comes back?
translation_hi: हे बाला लीलावती, हिरन के बच्चे जैसी चंचल आँखों वाली! हे कल्याणी, यदि तुम पूर्ण संख्या, स्थान, विभाग और खंड विधि से गुणा करने में कुशल हो, तो बताओ कि पाँच-तीन-एक वाली संख्या को 'सूर्यों' से गुणा करने पर क्या मिलता है? और उस गुणनफल को उसी गुणक से भाग देने पर क्या बचता है?
question: What is 135 × 12?
solution:
Whole (rupa): 135 × 12 = 1620

By places (sthana): 135 × 1 = 135 and 135 × 2 = 270, placed one step apart: 1350 + 270 = 1620

By factors (vibhaga): 12 = 3 × 4, so 135 × 3 = 405, then 405 × 4 = 1620

By parts (khanda): 12 = 8 + 4, so 135 × 8 + 135 × 4 = 1080 + 540 = 1620

Divided back by 12: 1620 ÷ 12 = 135

Science link: the 'factors' and 'parts' methods are the distributive and associative laws. Computers still multiply by splitting numbers into parts: Karatsuba's fast multiplication algorithm (1960) is a clever khanda method.
